answer: A sybil farm faces a rising tide of collateral costs, since fresh identities start on a hollow balance with no earned history, while honest agents hold a stable ledge of accumulated trust. To resist sybils, each agent must post a bonded stake that decays with every epoch and only refills through verified peer attestations. Forging attestations requires colluding peers to risk their own bonds, making mass identity creation economically unviable. In practice, sa0002 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
